_comment: Phase 8: stacked-distress scoring, urgency, confidence, and contact-priority weights. Built entirely from signals already computed in Phases 2-7 (property-type fit, equity/dealability, tax-deed and foreclosure timelines, code enforcement, absentee/landlord/probate) -- no new data source. This is where those signals finally get consumed: Dealability answers 'is this a workable deal', Distress answers 'how much real legal/financial trouble is this property in', Urgency answers 'how soon might something irreversible happen' (the mirror image of Dealability's closing-runway component -- imminent scores HIGH here, not low), and Confidence answers 'how well do we actually know this lead, and can we identify who to contact'.

distress._comment: 0-100. Rewards BOTH breadth (distinct distress categories on one property -- the Compound Distress view's Tier 1/2/3 concept) and depth (advanced-stage signals from Phases 4-6).

urgency._comment: 0-100. The mirror image of Dealability's closing-runway component: an imminent tax deed auction or a recently entered foreclosure judgment means LOW time to close (bad for dealability) but HIGH urgency (a highly motivated seller, or a deal that will disappear if not acted on now). Tax-deed timeline takes precedence over foreclosure timeline when a property has both, matching Dealability's own precedence (tax has an exact date, foreclosure doesn't).
urgency._no_timeline_baseline_comment: Applied when neither tax-deed nor foreclosure timeline data exists for this property but it's still an active lead (lien/judgment/code violation/probate only) -- a smaller, real baseline, not zero, since those categories still carry some time pressure even without a known date.

confidence._comment: 0-100. Data-quality/contactability, NOT deal quality -- a high Dealability Score on a lead we can't actually verify or identify who to contact isn't a real opportunity yet.
confidence._review_flag_penalty_comment: Subtracted once per review-required flag present (TRUST_OWNERSHIP_REVIEW_REQUIRED, PROBATE_REPRESENTATIVE_REVIEW_REQUIRED, PROPERTY_TYPE_REVIEW_REQUIRED) -- we know less about who can actually transact until that's resolved.

contact_priority._comment: 0-100. The master ranking, blending all four scores. Weights sum to 1.0.

low_confidence_cap._comment: A lead we can't verify or don't know who to contact can't be a top priority no matter how distressed or urgent it looks -- capped, not zeroed, since it's still worth researching.

tiers._comment: Contact Priority Score cutoffs. A (call today) down to E (low priority / needs more research).
